description.narrative:
In today's ever-changing digital landscape, the media face unprecedented shifts in how they operate, from newsgathering, production, to distribution and audience engagement, and are confronted with increasingly complex challenges in the information ecosystems. Without the capacity to adapt to rapid technological advancements, including artificial intelligence (AI), media institutions risk obsolescence, threatening the very foundations of independence, pluralism and viability. While larger media organizations are rapidly adopting digital technologies, many small and medium-sized outlets lack the capacity or resources to do so, which widens structural disparities within the media landscape.
The programme described in this work plan will strengthen the digital and AI competencies of media institutions of all types and sizes, ensuring they continue informing and connecting communities effectively and maintain their competitive edge in the AI era. It integrates a variety of initiatives to support the media in the areas of leadership strategy, ethical AI governance, and staff competencies to move media organizations from passive awareness of the AI evolution and ad hoc use to active agency. This approach anchors growth in the durable principles of editorial independence and transparency. Implementation focuses on equitable access to and effective use of digital and AI tools, leadership capacity, robust internal policies and governance frameworks, and context-sensitive partnerships.
